title: What can you do?
paragraphs: My name is Kamila Seitkali. I am a second-year student at West Kazakhstan University named after Makhambет Utemisov (WKU) in Uralsk. This semester, my English teacher gave our class an interesting task: "Write a short text about what you CAN do and what you CANNOT do." At first, I thought it was a simple task. But when I started writing, I realised that I have more skills than I thought!

Let me start with languages. I can speak three languages: Kazakh, Russian, and English. I can speak Kazakh and Russian very well because they are my native languages. My English is not perfect yet, but I can understand most conversations, and I can write emails and short essays. I can also read English books — slowly, but I can do it! My dream is to speak English as fluently as a native speaker.

I can also play the dombra — a traditional Kazakh musical instrument with two strings. I learned it when I was eight years old. My grandfather taught me. I can play about twenty traditional Kazakh songs. Unfortunately, I cannot play the piano or the guitar. But music is in my heart, and I want to learn the guitar next year.

My best friend at WKU is Amir Bekzhanov. He is from Aktobe and he is studying Computer Science. Amir is very talented. He can program in three languages: Python, Java, and C++. He can create websites and mobile applications. Amir can also fix any computer or phone. Everybody in our group calls him "The Tech Wizard!" He cannot cook anything except instant noodles, though — which makes us laugh every time.

Our classmate Zhibek is a dancer. She can perform traditional Kazakh dances beautifully. She can also do gymnastics and yoga. Zhibek trains for two hours every day after classes. Another classmate, Rustam, is an excellent football player. He can run very fast and he can kick the ball with both his right foot and his left foot. He can also swim and play volleyball.

At university, we have the opportunity to learn new skills. I am learning to drive a car — but I cannot drive yet! I also started cooking lessons because I cannot cook well. My mother is a wonderful cook, but I cannot even make a proper bowl of soup! I want to change that this year. Learning new skills is exciting and sometimes a little frightening, but it is always worth it.

There are some things I cannot do but I want to learn: I cannot draw well — my drawings look like something a small child made. I cannot sing in tune — my friends always ask me to stop! And I cannot wake up easily in the morning — 7:30 am classes are a real challenge for me. But these are my goals for self-improvement this year.

I believe that every person has special abilities. Some people can run fast, some can think creatively, some can talk to anyone and make friends easily. The most important thing is to know your strengths and to keep developing them. And if there is something you cannot do today — practise, be patient, and one day you will say: "I can!"

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Amir, can you help me with my computer? It's very slow.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Of course! I can look at it right now. What's the problem?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I don't know exactly. Can you fix it?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Yes, I can. It needs more memory. I can install it in ten minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: You're amazing! Can you teach me about computers too?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Sure! I can teach you the basics. Can you come on Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Yes, I can! Can we meet at the library?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Perfect. By the way, can you play the dombra? I heard you play!

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Yes, I can! I can play twenty songs. Can you play any instrument?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: No, I can't. I can't play music at all. But I can code!

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Ha! You can fix computers, but you can't cook or play music!

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: True! We all have different abilities. That's what makes us a good team!

vocab.definition: the skill or power to do something
vocab.example: Every person has special abilities.

vocab.definition: in a smooth, natural, and confident way
vocab.example: I want to speak English fluently.

vocab.definition: having a natural skill or ability in something
vocab.example: Amir is a very talented programmer.

vocab.definition: an object used to produce music
vocab.example: The dombra is a traditional Kazakh instrument.

vocab.definition: following customs and ideas that have existed for a long time
vocab.example: She can perform traditional Kazakh dances.

vocab.definition: a chance to do something good or useful
vocab.example: University gives us the opportunity to learn.

vocab.definition: a positive quality or skill that someone has
vocab.example: Know your strengths and develop them.

vocab.definition: to do something regularly to improve your skill
vocab.example: Practise every day and you will improve.

vocab.definition: able to produce new and interesting ideas

vocab.definition: to become or make something better
vocab.example: My main goal is to improve my English.

vocab.definition: something difficult that requires effort and determination

vocab.definition: relating to the country or language you were born into
vocab.example: My native language is Kazakh.

vocab.definition: used when you feel sad or disappointed about something
vocab.example: Unfortunately, I cannot play the piano.

vocab.definition: to grow or make something grow stronger over time
vocab.example: Keep developing your special abilities.

vocab.definition: a sport involving physical exercises that need balance
vocab.example: Zhibek can do gymnastics and yoga.

vocab.definition: a person who is extremely skilled at something
vocab.example: Everybody calls Amir "The Tech Wizard".

vocab.definition: making you feel afraid or nervous
vocab.example: Learning new skills is sometimes frightening.

vocab.definition: the correct musical pitch of a note or song
vocab.example: I cannot sing in tune at all!

vocab.definition: to do an activity such as a dance or music in front of people
vocab.example: She can perform traditional dances on stage.

vocab.definition: the process of making yourself better through your own efforts
vocab.example: These are my goals for self-improvement.

grammarNote: Модальный глагол CAN используется для выражения способности или умения что-то делать. Это один из самых важных глаголов в английском языке. После CAN всегда стоит инфинитив (основная форма глагола) БЕЗ "to". Глагол CAN одинаков для всех лиц — он никогда не меняет форму.

rows.example: I can swim very fast.
She can speak French and German.
They can dance traditional dances.
He can play five instruments.
We can help you with the project.
This phone can connect to any network.
I can't drive — I don't have a licence.
She can't cook, but she tries every day.
He can't sing at all — it's very funny!
We can't be late for the exam.
They can't speak Russian, only Kazakh.
My laptop can't connect to this Wi-Fi.
Can you help me with this exercise?
Can she play the piano? — Yes, she can!
Can they speak English fluently?
What can you do? Tell me about your skills.
How well can she dance? — Very well!
Why can't he cook? — He never learned.
✅ She can speak English. (NO -s after can!)
✅ I can swim. (NO "to" after can!)
✅ He can speak French. (NO -s on verb!)
✅ Can you help me? (NO "to" in questions!)

grammarTip:
CAN никогда не меняет форму: I can · She can · They can (НЕ "she cans"!)
После CAN всегда голый инфинитив: I can swim · She can dance (НЕ "can to swim", НЕ "can swimming"!)
Отрицание: can + not = cannot (formal) = can't (spoken)
CAN'T произносится /kɑːnt/ — очень чётко, не путай с "can" /kæn/ в вопросах.
